summary: Feed s095_single to IDS is degraded: 9.5% of frames are truncated (sliced to ~128 bytes), exceeding 5% threshold. IDS requires full payload for inspection, so detection coverage is reduced. All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, one-way, oversize, drops, overload, tunnels) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is configured with packet slicing / snap-length of ~128 bytes, cutting frames short to save bandwidth or tool capacity. 168 of 1770 frames (9.49%) are truncated, well above the 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true for signature and anomaly detection. Truncated frames lose L4 payload and application data, so IDS cannot match signatures, reassemble flows, or detect exploits hidden beyond the first 128 bytes.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires complete payload per tool profile; disabling slicing restores full frames for deep packet inspection and improves detection coverage.
